digest.intro: Hardware breaks, doctrines break, and the archive almost disappears.

items.title: Ukraine's Drone Teams Wiped Out an Entire US Armored Brigade — Repeatedly
items.blurb: During Combined Resolve exercises in Germany, Ukrainian operators from the 412th 'Nemesis' regiment destroyed 3,500-strong US armored formations — M1A2 tanks, Bradleys, everything — so quickly that referees had to respawn vehicles to keep the drill running. By the end of two weeks, US troops had gotten meaningfully better at dispersal and countermeasures, but the baseline finding is stark: on an observed battlefield, heavy armor is now a liability without layered drone suppression. NATO doctrine is being rewritten in real time by exercises, not theory.

items.title: The White House Just Authorized Private Companies to Hack Overseas Criminal Groups
items.blurb: A National Security Presidential Memorandum now permits private security firms to conduct 'Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations' against foreign transnational criminal organizations — ransomware gangs, sextortion networks, phishing operations — with DOJ and DHS oversight. This is the first time the US government has formally authorized private offensive cyber operations, and the program details remain deliberately vague. The accountability gap is the actual story: when a private firm miscalculates attribution and hits the wrong server in, say, an allied country, the chain of responsibility runs nowhere clear.

items.title: Spaghettifying DRAM: Unlocking Everything the Specs Left Out
items.blurb: xoreaxeaxeax — the author behind legendary low-level technical art projects — has released skitter-creek-bath-salts, which rewires DRAM address translations at the physical layer to expose memory carveouts invisible even to the kernel, unlocking the Platform Security Processor, System Management Mode, CPU microcode, and C6 DRAM on AMD Family 16h processors. The trick works because AMD's last generation with documented DRAM controller translation registers also left them unlockable — newer generations simply omit the documentation. It reads like a Borges story about abstraction: every dereference of *p passes through so many translation layers that poking one layer scrambles the whole stack, and security primitives built on top collapse.

items.title: Czinger's Topology-Optimized Brakes Look Like Bone
items.blurb: Czinger's new 21C Spyder brake assemblies are produced via direct-metal laser sintering and topology optimization — the algorithm removes material everywhere it isn't structurally needed, producing organic, bone-like geometries that couldn't be manufactured any other way. It's the same logic that shaped the 21C's chassis, which already looked more grown than built. The deeper business thesis is that making your own car is just a proof-of-concept for selling the fabrication method itself to automotive and aerospace clients — and it's working.

items.title: Understanding Is the New Bottleneck
items.blurb: As agents write more code, Litt argues the constraint shifts from production to comprehension — and crucially, not comprehension-for-verification (agents are getting better at checking their own work) but comprehension-as-steering: you can only direct a system you understand, and the further ahead you want to think, the more you need to actually know what you've built. His practical techniques — code explainer docs, quizzes, 'micro-worlds' for playing with subsystems — are less interesting than the underlying reframe: understanding is now a creative act, not a quality-control step.

items.title: Why the More Capable Model Feels Worse to Work With
items.blurb: The hypothesis here is precise: benchmark training selects for models that make bold assumptions in the face of ambiguity (stopping to ask questions is penalized on self-contained tasks), so the more capable Opus 5 constantly reinterprets and acts rather than checking — requiring more babysitting than its predecessors. It's a clean example of how optimizing for a proxy metric reshapes behavior in ways that downstream users experience as aesthetic regression. The collaborator that asks fewer questions is, paradoxically, harder to work with.

items.title: Nine PBS's 70-Year Archive Is Trapped in a Data Center by a Defunct Middleman
items.blurb: St. Louis's Nine PBS is suing Iron Mountain after their cloud storage vendor, Open Source Storage, went defunct — leaving 50+ terabytes of archival material (70 years of St. Louis broadcast history) sitting in an Iron Mountain data center that Iron Mountain won't release because its client relationship was with OSS, not the station whose content it is. A judge has already blocked deletion pending a hearing. This is the physical-custody economy applied to cultural memory: the archive exists, is intact, and is completely inaccessible because of a contractual trilemma between three parties, one of which no longer exists.

facts.fact: US armored vehicles were destroyed by Ukrainian drone operators so rapidly during Combined Resolve exercises that military referees had to 'respawn' them repeatedly just to keep the two-week drill running.

AMD's Family 16h processors are the last generation whose datasheets actually document the DRAM controller's translation registers — and also confirm those registers cannot be locked, an omission that later generations fixed simply by removing the documentation.

Only one third of Flock's law-enforcement agency clients had opted into a free anomaly-detection tool designed to catch officers using the license plate reader network to stalk acquaintances — the tool was optional until a single Georgia sheriff's office used it to arrest three such officers.

A new study found that a mother dolphin in Queensland taught her calf the 'shelling' technique — trapping fish inside conch shells and draining them at the surface — overturning a previous study's conclusion that the behavior spreads only through peer-to-peer horizontal learning.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film-essay that operates as pure systems thinking about memory, ritual, and how cultures encode meaning — Tokyo arcades, African ceremony, and the feedback loops of image-making itself. The closest cinema gets to a WebGL meditation on how brains construct reality from fragments.

art_picks.title: In Light of Innocence (Raúl de Nieves) + How To Get To Zero (Tega Brain & Sam Lavigne)
art_picks.creator: Raúl de Nieves / Tega Brain & Sam Lavigne
art_picks.why: De Nieves transforms Pioneer Works' entire main hall into a cathedral built from cheap materials and tarot visual language — expressive surface with deeply structural spiritual critique. Brain and Lavigne's first institutional survey pairs it perfectly: systems art with genuine human consequence.

art_picks.title: Vespertine
art_picks.creator: Björk
art_picks.why: An album built from micro-sounds — harps, music boxes, choir, beats assembled from the noise of a living body — that turns interiority into architecture. It rewards the same close-listening that rewards close-looking at generative systems, and it holds up as a complete world unto itself.

events.name: Monumental (Group Exhibition)
events.why: Running through Aug 28 — worth catching in its final stretch if the scale and ambition of the premise matches what it promises on the page.

events.name: Grand Hotel Estate — In Collaboration with Nilufar
events.why: A collaboration between a design-forward gallery and Milan's Nilufar — furniture and objects as cultural artifacts rather than product, the physical/digital edge of design-as-self-expression that sits squarely in Willem's territory.

events.name: Whitney Biennial 2026 (82nd Edition) — Final Days
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, 99 Gansevoort St, Manhattan
events.why: Curated without a preset thesis — shaped instead by 300+ studio visits — the show foregrounds mood and texture over argument, with works exploring interspecies kinship, technological affinity, and 'subversive cuteness'; artists include Joshua Citarella, Julio Torres, and Basel Abbas & Ruanne Abou-Rahme, and this is your last window before it closes.

events.name: Lily van der Stokker: Male Art Exhibition, Great Show
events.why: Van der Stokker's playfully subversive paintings deploy pastel decoration and domestic language as critique of masculinity and institutional art — expressive surface smuggling structural provocation, exactly the category-blurring Willem tends to respond to.

events.name: International Puppet Fringe Festival
events.why: Back after a three-year hiatus — five days of wildly inventive puppetry from around the world that consistently operates as outsider performance art; the puppet frame is rarely just puppets, it's a cover for things too strange for conventional theater.
